instruction: Read only the public problem and document. Recover the distinct reasoning steps actually advocated, in your own concise ordinary English. A step links a stated or clearly implied reason to a concrete mechanism/action and its intended consequence. Keep roles, ordering, conditions and scope. Do not fill in unstated reasoning. Separate distinct causal applications, merge duplicates, and abstain on unsupported or unresolved ones. Return any number of steps. For each give premise, action, consequence, and quote (one exact contiguous source passage supporting the step). Use [] if none. No fixed vocabulary or reference answers are supplied.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A cupboard fills faster than a hall committee expects when the first donations arrive in moving boxes. Measure its shelves with actual puzzle boxes and set an intake limit that leaves room to lift them out.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: People arriving specifically to contribute may leave boxes in a corridor when the hall is closed. Advertise a staffed intake window and explain where to bring a puzzle during that time.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A person who has never owned a jigsaw is an obvious first borrower. Let anyone take one during opening hours and present donations as a way to replenish the shelf over time.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A neighbor may interpret taking a puzzle as a promise to return that exact box. Explain on the shelf sign that puzzles can be kept, passed along or brought back after somebody finishes them.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A familiar brand can reuse a box design across several piece counts. Label each donated puzzle with its title and stated count from the manufacturer's panel so people can compare likely commitments.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Piece count alone gives a poor indication of the table space a puzzle needs. Copy the finished dimensions onto the shelf card so a resident can check whether a kitchen table will suffice.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A thousand-piece puzzle with distinct illustrated characters feels different from a thousand pieces of sky. Let contributors add a plain description of the image and the stretches that made their build challenging.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A donor who finished a puzzle last weekend has different information from someone clearing an attic. Record whether the donor completed it, knows of a missing piece or has never checked the contents.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: People vary in how much a missing piece bothers them. Keep playable incomplete puzzles together and show the known gap on the box image with a removable note so takers can decide.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Boxes come open when they are tilted out of a tight stack. Ask intake volunteers to put loose pieces into a resealable bag and close it before placing the box on the shelf.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Two unmarked bags on a sorting table can lead to an accidental mixture. Handle one open box at a time and close its bag before assessing the next donation.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: An already assembled jigsaw is easier to take down when large sections are turned over first. Invite the last builder to check the backs and separate connected pieces before donating it for a fresh solve.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: People with limited grip may find small, thickly packed pieces awkward to handle. Mark large-piece sets by their actual piece size and keep a sample outline on their cards for comparison.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A small child may reach whatever is on the bottom shelf while a caregiver browses. Reserve that space for boxed children's puzzles and keep the original age guidance visible on each one.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: An image printed on the lid may be the only reference available while assembling. Check that the picture is legible and include a clean image from the donor when a damaged lid needs a substitute.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A faded or crushed box can hide a perfectly good puzzle. Transfer it to a firm container if the pieces and reference image are usable, and carry over the title, dimensions and condition note.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Damp cardboard can spoil the boxes beside it once a cupboard closes. Examine incoming boxes in good light and ask the donor to take back any that show moisture or mildew.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: People may forget a puzzle's title by the time they discover a problem at home. Give accepted boxes a short identifier so a resident can report an issue without trying to describe the artwork.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: When a reported missing piece turns up under the dining table, a whole puzzle can become complete again. Keep found pieces in labeled envelopes behind the desk and match them using the puzzle identifier.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Takers become the best source of fresh condition reports after a puzzle leaves the hall. Include a small card they can update after assembly and pass on with the box to its next home.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A collection with many similar landscapes can look larger than its real choice of subjects. Group the boxes by image and rotate the front-facing selection so less familiar themes get seen.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Volunteers need a way to tell high turnover from slow accumulation. Tally incoming and outgoing boxes during each opening and use the trend to decide when the next donation window can fit.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: A crowded shelf can discourage browsing while the same few boxes remain untouched. Date each arrival and move the oldest titles to a clearly marked giveaway table during a hall event.

documents.problem: A residents' group has a cupboard at the community hall and wants to start a free jigsaw puzzle exchange. How could neighbors give and take puzzles with confidence while keeping the collection manageable?
documents.text: Neighbors sometimes need to picture a completed puzzle before they choose it. Invite builders to contribute a snapshot for a noticeboard and put its box identifier underneath so someone can look for the same one.
